related_questions.question: How serious is catching COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help. In some people, severe COVID-19 illness can lead to death.

related_questions.question: How long do I have to wait after being exposed to COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: After COVID-19 exposure, it's recommended to wait at least five days before testing to get the most accurate results. If you're not fully vaccinated, you should quarantine immediately, isolate at home, and watch for symptoms like fever, shortness of breath, or other COVID-19 symptoms, according to Norton Healthcare. If you test negative but were exposed, consider taking two more tests, 48 hours apart, to confirm the result. If you test positive at any time, assume the result is accurate.

related_questions.question: Is the COVID pandemic still going on?

text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, COVID-19 continues to circulate. The pandemic's official end is not clearly defined, and whether it's still considered a pandemic depends on the definition used. Currently, COVID-19 vaccines continue to offer protection against severe disease and death according to the WHO.

related_questions.question: How many times will I get COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People can be reinfected with SARS-CoV-2 multiple times. Each time a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, they have a risk of developing Long COVID. Long COVID symptoms and conditions can emerge, persist, resolve, and reemerge over weeks and months.
